testCase.description: DMN 1.6 §10.3.2.15 descendant-expression mapping table (after Table 68, p.136) (rule 68, normative example): "{ a: { b: { b: 1 } } }...b is evaluated to: [ { b: 1 }, 1 ] because each key contained in the context and all of its nested contexts are returned as a list of associated values".

DMN 1.6 §10.3.2.15 descendant-expression mapping table (after Table 68, p.136): the descendant expression returns "a list of associated values"; derived from the normative example: ({ a: { b: { b: 1 } } }...b)[2] = 1.

DMN 1.6 §10.3.2.15 descendant-expression mapping table (after Table 68, p.136): "each key contained in the context ... returned as a list of associated values"; derived: a single top-level match still yields a list, { b: 1 }...b = [1].

DMN 1.6 §10.3.2.15 descendant-expression mapping table (after Table 68, p.136): "each key contained in the context and all of its nested contexts"; derived from the normative example: the value of a matching entry is itself searched, outer match first: [ { b: { b: 1 } }, { b: 1 }, 1 ].

DMN 1.6 §10.3.2.15 descendant-expression mapping table (after Table 68, p.136): "access a property name recursively throughout the nested context"; derived: a match three levels deep is found, result ["x"].

DMN 1.6 §10.3.2.15 descendant-expression mapping table (after Table 68, p.136): "each key contained in the context and all of its nested contexts are returned as a list of associated values"; derived: matches in two sibling nested contexts are both returned. The order of sibling matches is not specified (§10.3.2.6: a context is a "partially ordered collection"), so the result is sorted: sort({ a: { b: 1 }, c: { b: 2 } }...b, function(x, y) x < y) = [1, 2].

DMN 1.6 §10.3.2.15 descendant-expression mapping table (after Table 68, p.136): "returned as a list of associated values"; derived: a matching value that is a list is one associated value, so it is returned as one item (not flattened), and the non-matching entry a: 1 contributes nothing: { a: 1, c: { b: [3, 4] } }...b = [[3, 4]].

DMN 1.6 §10.3.2.15 descendant-expression mapping table (after Table 68, p.136): "each key contained in the context and all of its nested contexts are returned as a list of associated values"; derived: no entry named b anywhere gives the empty list [].
DMN 1.6 §10.3.2.15 descendant-expression mapping table (after Table 68, p.136): applicability "type e is a context"; derived: the empty context is a context with no matching keys, result [].

DMN 1.6 §10.3.2.15 descendant-expression mapping table (after Table 68, p.136): "returned as a list of associated values"; derived: a matching entry whose value is null contributes null, result [null].

DMN 1.6 §10.3.1.2 grammar rule 68 "descendant expression = expression , "..." , name" and DMN 1.6 §10.3.2.15 descendant-expression mapping table (after Table 68, p.136); derived: the name may contain spaces, result ["x"].

DMN 1.6 §10.3.2.15 descendant-expression mapping table (after Table 68, p.136): applicability "type e is a context"; §10.3.2.15: "Inputs outside of their domain result in a null value". A string is not a context, so "abc"...b is null.

DMN 1.6 §10.3.2.15 descendant-expression mapping table (after Table 68, p.136): applicability "type e is a context"; §10.3.2.15: "Inputs outside of their domain result in a null value". A boolean is not a context, so true...b is null.

DMN 1.6 §10.3.2.15 descendant-expression mapping table (after Table 68, p.136): applicability "type e is a context"; §10.3.2.15: "Inputs outside of their domain result in a null value". null is not a context, so null...b is null.

DMN 1.6 §10.3.2.15 descendant-expression mapping table (after Table 68, p.136): "access a property name recursively throughout the nested context" (DMN16-72 use case: deep input data); derived: message...name over typed input data returns both names; sibling order is not specified (§10.3.2.6 "partially ordered collection"), so the result is sorted: sort(message...name, function(x, y) x < y) = ["Ann", "Bob"].

DMN 1.6 §10.3.1.4: "A FEEL expression consists of a sequence of tokens, possibly separated with white space" and "..." is a literal terminal symbol of grammar rule 68 "descendant expression = expression , "..." , name"; derived: white space around "..." does not change the result, { b: 1 } ... b = [1].

DMN 1.6 §10.3.2.6: "In the syntax, keys can be either names or strings. Keys are mapped to strings in the semantic domain", with the §10.3.2.15 descendant-expression mapping table (after Table 68, p.136), e...name mapped to e..."name"; derived: string keys match the name, outer match first as in the normative example: { "b": { "b": 2 } }...b = [ { b: 2 }, 2 ].

DMN 1.6 §10.3.2.15 descendant-expression mapping table (after Table 68, p.136) with Table 69 (filter on a list of contexts) and §10.3.1.5 (path over a list); derived DMN16-72 use case: find a party at any depth, filter it by role, then take its name: ({ deal: { party: { role: "Appraiser", name: "Ann" } } }...party)[role = "Appraiser"].name = ["Ann"].
